messages.content: You are a precise information extraction system. You only output valid JSON.

Extract entities, events and event arguments from the document.

Entity types:
- Person: a named or described human individual or group of people
- Organization: a company, army, government body, team, party or other organised group
- Location: a geographic place: country, city, region, body of water, battlefield, etc.
- Building: a man-made structure or facility: hotel, fort, bridge, airport, etc.
- Product: a man-made object or product: vehicle, ship, aircraft, weapon model, etc.
- Art: a creative work: book, film, song, painting, etc.
- Other: any other named thing relevant to events (e.g. nationalities, named events, ideologies)

Entity annotation rules:
- Annotate named entities AND other mentions that refer to them: nominal phrases ("the plane", "the storm"), subject/object pronouns ("he", "she", "they", "him"), and nationality/group words ("British", "Ottomans").
- Do NOT annotate possessive pronouns ("his", "her", "their", "its"), dates or years ("3 January 1992", "2013").
- Numbers, quantities, ordinals and durations ("13", "two", "3rd", "two days") are entities of type Other.
- Annotate every occurrence, including repeated mentions of the same entity.
- Nationality or group words are typed by what they refer to: a country/place -> Location, an army/state/organisation -> Organization, a people -> Person.

Event types:
- Attack: An agent physically assaults or launches a violent attack on a target (bombing, ambush, raid, shooting, assault). (e.g. attack, assaulted, ambushed, bombing)
- Military_operation: Organised armed conflict between forces: a war, battle, campaign, siege or military operation as a whole. (e.g. war, battle, fought, campaign)
- Conquering: An agent takes control of a place or group by force (capture, seize, conquer, occupy). (e.g. captured, conquer, seized, taken)
- Killing: A killer causes the death of a victim (an agent is responsible for the death). (e.g. killed, killing, murdered, massacre)
- Death: Someone dies, with focus on the death itself rather than on a killer. (e.g. died, death, dead, deaths)
- Bodily_harm: Someone is physically injured or wounded. (e.g. injured, wounded, injuries, hurt)
- Catastrophe: A natural or man-made disaster happens (storm, flood, earthquake, crash, fire, accident). (e.g. hurricane, storm, flood, earthquake)
- Destroying: Something is destroyed completely (destroyed, demolished, sunk, burned down). (e.g. destroyed, destruction, demolished, sank)
- Damaging: Something is damaged but not completely destroyed. (e.g. damage, damaged, struck, battered)
- Statement: A speaker communicates a message (says, states, announces, describes, reports). (e.g. said, stated, announced, described)
- Change_of_leadership: Leadership or control of a polity or organisation changes (election, coup, revolution, ousting, independence, replacement of a leader). (e.g. elected, coup, revolution, ousted)
- Arriving: An agent arrives at or reaches a place. (e.g. arrived, reached, entered, landed)

Trigger annotation rules:
- A trigger is the single word (sometimes a short phrase) that most clearly expresses the event; it can be a verb ("attacked") or a noun ("attack", "war", "fires").
- Annotate EVERY occurrence: if the same event is mentioned several times ("the fires ... the fires ..."), list each occurrence as a separate entry.
- Only annotate the 12 event types below; ignore other kinds of events.
- Disambiguation:
  * Military_operation = a war, battle, campaign or siege as a whole; Attack = one specific assault, bombing, raid, shelling or ambush.
  * Conquering = capturing or taking control of a place or group (captured, seized, took, defeated and occupied).
  * Killing = someone or something kills (killed, massacre, slain, executed); Death = the dying itself (died, death, dead, fatalities).
  * Catastrophe = the disaster event itself (storm, hurricane, fire, flood, crash, accident); Destroying = something is completely destroyed; Damaging = something is damaged but not destroyed.
  * Bodily_harm = injury or wounding (injured, wounded, injuries).

Argument roles:
Event type Attack: An agent physically assaults or launches a violent attack on a target (bombing, ambush, raid, shooting, assault).
Roles:
- Agent: the attacker
- Patient: the target being attacked
- Location: where the attack happens
- Consequence: the result of the attack (e.g. casualties, what was gained)

Argument annotation rules:
- Arguments may be anywhere in the document, not only in the trigger's sentence.
- Copy the SHORTEST span that fully identifies the argument: prefer a name ("Seneca") over a longer phrase ("the Seneca in particular"); for people counts keep the number phrase ("30 such individuals").
- A role may have several arguments; omit a role if the document does not mention it.
- Consequence/Loss/Message/Details roles are usually clauses or longer phrases; copy them as written.

### Example 2
Document:
On November 5, 2009, a mass shooting took place at Fort Hood, near Killeen, Texas. Nidal Hasan, a U.S. Army major and psychiatrist, fatally shot 13 people and injured more than 30 others. It was the deadliest mass shooting on an American military base. Hasan was shot and as a result paralyzed from the waist down. Hasan was arraigned by a military court on July 20, 2011 and was charged with 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted murder under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. His court-martial began on August 7, 2013. Due to the nature of the charges (more than one premeditated, or first-degree, murder case, in a single crime), Hasan faced either the death penalty or life in prison without parole upon conviction. Hasan was found guilty on 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted premeditated murder on August 23, 2013, and was sentenced to death on August 28, 2013. days after the shooting, reports in the media revealed that a joint terrorism task force had been aware of a series of e-mails between hasan and the unk imam anwar al-awlaki, who had been monitored by the nsa as a security threat, and that hasan's colleagues had been aware of his increasing radicalization for several years. the failure to prevent the shootings led the defense department and the fbi to commission investigations, and congress to hold hearings. The U.S. government declined requests from survivors and family members of the slain to categorize the Fort Hood shooting as an act of terrorism, or motivated by militant Islamic religious convictions. In November 2011, a group of survivors and family members filed a lawsuit against the government for negligence in preventing the attack, and to force the government to classify the shootings as terrorism. The Pentagon argued that charging Hasan with terrorism was not possible within the military justice system and that such action could harm the military prosecutors ' ability to sustain a guilty verdict against Hasan.

### Example 3
Document:
The McMahon killings or the McMahon murders occurred on 24 March 1922 when six Catholic civilians were shot dead at the home of the McMahon family in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Gunmen broke into their house at night and shot all eight males inside, in an apparent sectarian attack. The victims were businessman Owen McMahon, four of his sons, and one of his employees. Two others were shot but survived, and a female family member was assaulted. The survivors said that most of the gunmen wore police uniforms and it is suspected that they were members of the Ulster Special Constabulary. It is believed to have been a reprisal for the Irish Republican Army's (IRA) killing of two policemen the day before. Northern Ireland had been created ten months before, in the midst of the Irish War of Independence. A truce ended the war in most of Ireland; but a sectarian conflict in Belfast, and fighting in border areas, continued. Northern Ireland's police forces – especially the USC, which was almost exclusively Protestant and unionist – were implicated in a number of attacks on Catholic and Irish nationalist civilians as reprisal for IRA actions. A week later, six more Catholics were killed in another reprisal attack.

the white house farm murders took place near the village of tolleshunt d'arcy, essex, england, during the night of unk august 1985. Nevill and June Bamber were shot and killed inside their farmhouse, along with their adoptive daughter, Sheila Caffell, and Sheila's six-year-old twin sons, Daniel and Nicholas Caffell. The only surviving member of June and Nevill's immediate family was their adoptive son, Jeremy Bamber, then 24 years old, who said he had been at home a few miles away when the shooting took place. The police at first believed that Sheila, diagnosed with schizophrenia, had fired the shots then turned the gun on herself. But weeks after the murders Jeremy Bamber's ex-girlfriend told police that he had implicated himself. The prosecution argued that, motivated by a large inheritance, Bamber had shot the family with his father's semi-automatic rifle, then placed the gun in his unstable sister's hands to make it look like a murder–suicide. A silencer the prosecution said was on the rifle would have made it too long, they argued, for Sheila's fingers to reach the trigger to shoot herself. Bamber was convicted of five counts of murder in October 1986 by a 10–2 majority, sentenced to a minimum of 25 years, and informed in 1994 that he would never be released. The Court of Appeal upheld the verdict in 2002. Bamber protested his innocence throughout, although his extended family remained convinced of his guilt. between 2004 and 2012, his lawyers submitted several unsuccessful applications to the criminal cases review commission. They argued that the silencer might not have been used during the killings, that the crime scene may have been damaged then reconstructed, that crime-scene photographs were taken weeks after the murders, and that the time of Sheila's death had been miscalculated. A key issue was whether Bamber received a call from his father that night to say Sheila had " gone berserk " with a gun. Bamber said that he did, that he alerted police, and that Sheila fired the final shot while he and the officers were standing outside the house. It became a central plank of the prosecution's case that the father had made no such call, and that the only reason Bamber would have lied about it—indeed, the only way he could have known about the shootings when he alerted the police—was that he was the killer himself.
